SPEC / E5 CONTRACT DELTAS: (a) after an abandon, a supplier refusal or an AUTHORIZATION_FAILED the void rule (c3) moves the orders to fulfilment 'cancelled', so Order.presentation is 'cancelled', as test/fixtures/contracts/plan-abandon.json shows; 'cancelled_payment_incomplete' (F-TR-11) appears for an order whose plan is non_executable while its fulfilment is still confirmed, i.e. after the execute claim (CAPTURE_FAILED, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED at step 2, e4) or when a plan is set non_executable without the rule; the fixture payments/view-non-executable.json shows that second state under the title 'abandoned', which the real abandon does not produce (e5's assumption 3 holds for the post-claim case only). (b) e5 assumption 1 (details.requestIds in RESERVATION_LIMIT) is not delivered: it is in src/services/reservations.js, not an e2 file; the UI's fallback works. (c) assumption 2 holds: Order.payment.status exposes approved, authorization_pending, unknown and the other machine states. (d) assumption 4 holds: approvalUrl is the adapter's http(s) link. (e) assumption 5 is e4's. (f) Payment.approvalUrl is null once the status is not 'created' or a cancellation was requested (the fixtures already show null there). (g) Redirect outcomes: paypal=returned, paypal=cancelled, paypal=not_approved (order not APPROVED at the provider, or getOrder rejected), paypal=check_failed (getOrder retryable/unknown); the UI renders notices only for returned and cancelled. (h) A missing or malformed ?token is 400 BAD_REQUEST (spec silent); a supplier or admin session on return/cancel is 403 FORBIDDEN (RBAC matrix); the anonymous cancel redirects to /#/signin?notice=paypal-return like the return. (i) abandon of an already abandoned plan (PAYMENT_CANCELLED) is 200 with the current state (state-idempotence convention); any other non-approved plan is 409 INVALID_STATE. (j) paypal/create 502 PROVIDER_ERROR carries details.issue (an upper-case issue code only). (k) paypal/create is not rate-limited beyond the general per-user limit (300/min); no stricter limit was specified.

CALLS API (src/services/calls.js): queueCall(db, clock, {operationId, supplierOrderId, kind, attempt, requestId?}) inside the business transaction; startCall(db, clock, id, {guard, resendUnknown}) returns {token, call, op} or null; recordCall(env, {callId, token, outcome, apply, fence}) -> {fenced} | {fenced:false, followUp}, apply({db, clock, env, call, op, outcome, now}) maps the result inside the record transaction (e4: capture, with guard = lease check at start and fence = plan epoch at record); runCall(env, id, {resendUnknown}) for create_order/authorize/void/refund; sendDueCalls(env, {kinds, limit}) for reconciler step 6; flushQueuedVoids; resolveRejectedVoid(env, opId) (idempotent, may be called again for an authorized operation with void_failed and a cancel request); moveOperation(db, clock, op, to, set) (CAS + state table), restoreFromUnknown(db, clock, op) for resolution; loadOperation. SENDER TABLE as implemented: create_order = the paypal/create handler and the buyer's next call (never the reconciler); authorize = the return handler right after its commit, then sendDueCalls while the operation is approved and cancel_requested_at is NULL (a cancelled one is voided locally by the void rule); void = the app flushes the port's pending keys before the request that queued them answers, then sendDueCalls; refund = runCall by the compensation caller, then sendDueCalls; capture = lease holder only (e4). A refund start moves refund_requested -> refund_pending; the mapped refund results are in calls.js. RESOLUTION HOOK: e3 (webhook) and e4 (reconciler resolution, pending poll) call ctx.voidRule.onAuthorized(db, {operationId, requestId}) in the same transaction as any move into authorized; the compensation hook for captured is e4's. FAKE FAULTS used by tests: INSERT INTO fault_flags (name, value, remaining, created_at) with name fake_paypal:<fault> (value = supplier code or empty); http_429:<kind> is retryable, http_4xx is rejected, lost_response:<kind> is unknown with the effect applied. TEST SHAPE: tests install the real port with h.app.deps.voidRule = createVoidRule({clock: h.clock, provider: createVoidPort({clock: h.clock})}); the buyer approves the fake order with a POST to <approvalUrl>/approve (303 to http://localhost:<appPort>/api/paypal/return?token=[REDACTED]; the Sandbox variant starts startPaypalStub() and the harness with RS_PAYMENT_PROVIDER=paypal-sandbox, RS_PAYPAL_BASE_URL=<stub.baseUrl> and the DEFAULT credentials (single-credential mode, merchant key DEFAULT).

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson applies to a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root in a repository with several records; this task builds payment services, routes and API tests and designs no hook, guard or root discovery, so its 'Applies when' list does not hold. The guard accepted every nested write here and refused only an inline python file writer, asking for the Edit tool.
